old.name: Anxoves de l'Escala — Solés (1888) & Callol i Serrats (1847)
old.text: Anchovy salters, L'Escala (Alt Empordà) Two family salting houses curing 'Anxoves de l'Escala' in salt and hand-filleting them; Solés founded 1888, Fills de J. Callol i Serrats founded 1847. Callol i Serrats runs factory visits for groups and individuals; both have shops in L'Escala. Tour booking via the producers / Visit L'Escala tourism office.

old.name: Empordàlia (Oli de Pau + DO Empordà wines)
old.hook: Cooperative — wine and DOP olive oil, Pau & Vilajuïga
old.text: Cooperative — wine and DOP olive oil, Pau & Vilajuïga Cooperative formed 2005 from the Pau (1961) and Vilajuïga (1947) co-ops. Makes DO Empordà wines and Oli de Pau extra-virgin oil from the local argudell and corivell olives off ~500 ha of old groves. Oil-mill and winery visits with tastings, plus a farm shop at Pau and Vilajuïga; book via empordalia.com.

old.name: Celler Martín Faixó (Perafita / Cadac)
old.hook: Winery with vines ON Cap de Creus, by Cadaqués (slate, tramuntana)
old.text: Winery with vines ON Cap de Creus, by Cadaqués (slate, tramuntana) Family estate at Mas Sa Perafita, founded 2000 (first wines 2007), 11 ha on slate inside the natural park; labels Perafita and Cadac. Wine tourism since 2010: guided vineyard visits, tastings, pairings, vineyard hikes and rural-hotel stays. Booking by appointment via martinfaixo.com (phone listed on site as +34 972 258 954 — verify before relying on it). Road to Cadaqués, 17488 Cadaqués.

old_also.name: Cap de Creus slate wine — Martín Faixó (Perafita / Cadac)
old_also.hook: The one winery with vines actually on the Cap de Creus peninsula by Cadaqués.
old_also.text: The one winery with vines actually on the Cap de Creus peninsula by Cadaqués. €€–€€€ Family estate (Rafa & Carme Martín; daughter Ester winemaker), founded 2000, first wines 2007. 11 ha of vines on slate between Cadaqués, Roses and Port de la Selva, inside Cap de Creus Natural Park; varieties incl. Garnatxa, Cabernet, Merlot, Picapoll, Muscat of Alexandria. Labels Perafita and Cadac. An underground winery, fought over for ~20 years of permits, was set to begin in 2026. NOTE: bottle output is reported as 50,000 (estate site) and 70,000 (ARA interview) — figure unverified. Producers: Celler Martín Faixó (Mas Sa Perafita, Cadaqués)

old.name: Mas Estela
old.hook: Biodynamic winery, La Selva de Mar (Alt Empordà)
old.text: Biodynamic winery, La Selva de Mar (Alt Empordà) Soto-Dalmau family estate in the Sant Romà valley; ~50 ha bought 1989, organic from the start and biodynamic since 1999. Brands Vinya Selva de Mar, Quindals (some aged in clay amphorae), Moscatell Estela, Estela Dolç. Visits/tastings by arrangement via masestela.com; book ahead.

old.name: Espelt Viticultors
old.text: Large DO Empordà estate, Vilajuïga One of the biggest Empordà estates, with Garnatxa, Carinyena and Lledoner across the Alt Empordà. Listed by DO Empordà; visits by appointment (~2.5 h, around €27 with tasting per DO/visit listings — confirm current price), tours in Catalan, Spanish, English and French. Book via the winery.

old.name: Cami de Ronda: Platja de Cadaques to Far de Cala Nans
old.hook: The bay's eastern lip, white houses then bare schist, ending at an 1874 lighthouse.
chips: 3.6 km one way, about 1h15 each way (around 8 km / 2h50 return)
Late afternoon for the light on the white village; avoid days of hard tramuntana
old.text: The bay's eastern lip, white houses then bare schist, ending at an 1874 lighthouse. 3.6 km one way, about 1h15 each way (around 8 km / 2h50 return) Late afternoon for the light on the white village; avoid days of hard tramuntana From trail marker AE-141 at the south end of the village the path threads past Punta des Baluard, the Port de l'Alguer and Punta d'en Pampa before the houses give out and the route runs into open Cap de Creus rock as far as the Cala Nans light, inaugurated 1 September 1874, its lamp 36 m above the sea with a range of 8 nautical miles. Rated easy; rock-entry swimming below the far, no beach. Full exposure to the tramuntana on the headland. Open in Google Maps →

old_also.name: Cala Nans (Far de Cala Nans)
old_also.text: Coastal path on foot from the centre, 3.6 km / about 1h15 each way from trail marker AE-141; rock-entry swimming, no beach A rocky inlet at the far eastern end of the bay below the 1874 lighthouse (light 36 m above the sea, range 8 nautical miles); schist ledges to swim off, fully exposed to the tramuntana Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Cadaques to the Ermita de Sant Sebastia (Peni viewpoint)
old.hook: A thyme-and-rosemary climb to the balcony over the whole bay.
chips: Early morning before the heat for the climb; clear days for the Roses-bay and Pyrenees views
old.text: A thyme-and-rosemary climb to the balcony over the whole bay. About 8 km, +350 m, roughly 2h30 Early morning before the heat for the climb; clear days for the Roses-bay and Pyrenees views From the village the path climbs the eastern flank of Puig Peni through scrub of thyme, rosemary and rockrose to the 18th-century hermitage of Sant Sebastia de Peni, sited at about 385 m and held in private hands since 1890 (its romeria falls every 20 January). The bay of Cadaques, the coves below and Cala Nans with its lighthouse open up underfoot. The Peni summit proper (606 m) carries the EVA-4 military radar and is closed to the public, so this hermitage is the viewpoint to aim for. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Cami Antic: Portlligat to the Far de Cap de Creus
old.hook: The old path cove-to-cove to the easternmost lighthouse on the Iberian peninsula.
chips: 5.54 km one way / about 2h20 (roughly 14.8 km / 4h return from Cadaques)
Morning start to reach the cape before the midday crowds; clear days for the Pyrenees-to-sea panorama
old.text: The old path cove-to-cove to the easternmost lighthouse on the Iberian peninsula. 5.54 km one way / about 2h20 (roughly 14.8 km / 4h return from Cadaques) Morning start to reach the cape before the midday crowds; clear days for the Pyrenees-to-sea panorama Start at the AE-252 junction on the Portlligat beach; the route crosses the road to Cala Es Jonquet and Platja de Sant Lluis, reaches Guillola beach and the Cami Antic turnoff, then climbs through abandoned vineyard and olive terraces with the lighthouse always on the skyline. Yellow paint marks the way. The Far del Cap de Creus light entered service the night of 29 July 1853, the second oldest in Catalonia, marking the easternmost point of mainland Spain. Open in Google Maps →

old_also.name: The olive-terrace path (Cami Antic through the abandoned vinyes)
old_also.hook: Dry-stone terraces of dead vineyards, now sage, thyme and olive, framing the lighthouse.
chips: About 45 min of the path section to the lighthouse; part of the 14.8 km / 4 h Cami Antic return
Spring for flowering rockrose and broom on the terraces; soft light late afternoon
old_also.text: Dry-stone terraces of dead vineyards, now sage, thyme and olive, framing the lighthouse. About 45 min of the path section to the lighthouse; part of the 14.8 km / 4 h Cami Antic return Spring for flowering rockrose and broom on the terraces; soft light late afternoon The middle section of the Cami Antic, once past Guillola beach, climbs through orchards of sage, thyme and olive trees on the abandoned dry-stone vineyard terraces that once carried the Garnatxa and Carinyena vines of this coast, the Cap de Creus lighthouse profile held in the distance the whole way. The slate walls, built by hand against the slope, are the human grain of the peninsula's schist. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Cap de Creus lighthouse + Cala Culip loop
old.hook: Park at the cape, drop to a sheltered cove over Roman wrecks, climb back to the light.
chips: About 4 km loop, 1.5-2 h with a swim
Late morning when the sun is on the cove water; avoid rough-sea days
old.text: Park at the cape, drop to a sheltered cove over Roman wrecks, climb back to the light. About 4 km loop, 1.5-2 h with a swim Late morning when the sun is on the cove water; avoid rough-sea days From the lighthouse car park a 10-minute slope path drops to Cala Culip, a 15 m shingle cove sheltered from the tramuntana with a snorkel-able seabed holding ancient wrecks (Culip IV, c. 70-80 AD). The short Paratge de Tudela-Cala Culip circuit runs about 4 km. Leave the lighthouse path and step a few dozen metres right to look down on the cove; Cala Jugadora and Cala Fredosa sit just south. Open in Google Maps →

old_also.name: Cala Culip
old_also.text: By car to the Cap de Creus lighthouse (8 km / 20 min) then 10 min down the slope, or on foot via the Cami de Ronda in about 1h30 Tiny 15 m shingle-and-rock cove at the foot of the lighthouse, sheltered and clear; sponges, starfish and moray on the snorkel, and seabed of ancient wrecks (Culip IV, c. 70-80 AD) Open in Google Maps →

old.name: GR-92 Cami de Ronda stretch: Cadaques to El Port de la Selva
old.hook: The long-distance coast path over the spine of the peninsula to the next bay.
chips: About 12 km, roughly 3 h one way to El Port de la Selva
Cooler months or an early start; carry water, there is no shade or service on the ridge
old.text: The long-distance coast path over the spine of the peninsula to the next bay. About 12 km, roughly 3 h one way to El Port de la Selva Cooler months or an early start; carry water, there is no shade or service on the ridge The GR-92 runs the length of the Catalan coast from Portbou to Ulldecona; the Cadaques leg heads inland and uphill on stony paths across the Cap de Creus reserve to El Port de la Selva, with the Sant Pere de Rodes monastery and Sant Salvador de Verdera in reach on the longer circuit. A demanding stage of bare schist, wind-bent vegetation and big sea views rather than a stroll. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Platja Gran de Cadaques
old.text: In the centre, straight off the seafront promenade by the Dali statue The 200 m x 20 m town beach, coarse sand over pebbles, easy entry and the busiest stretch in summer; faces the open bay so the tramuntana pushes chop straight in Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Es Sortell
old.text: On foot about 1 km south past Sa Conca, parking roughly 300 m above Small 50 m grey gravel-and-rock cove with a stone footbridge out to the Sortell islet and pines wedged in the schist; shallow, calm, some of the best views back at the white village Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Platja de Sa Conca
old.text: On foot 15-20 min south along the shore promenade from the centre, or by car with a small lot above 100 m half-moon of coarse sand and pebbles, rocky seabed that drops off quickly; long nudist tradition and home of the Cadaques International Music Festival since 1970 Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Platja de Portlligat
old.text: On foot 15-20 min north over the hill from Cadaques centre, or 5 min by car with parking at the bay 170 m of grey shingle and cobble (no sand), facing east across the still bay that fronts Dali's house at Portlligat; sheltered water, full of moored fishing boats Open in Google Maps →

old.name: S'Alqueria Gran
old.text: By car about 2 km on the Cap de Creus lighthouse road then a short walk down; no dedicated parking About 60 m of pebbles and coarse sand in the Raco des Mor bay, no services, clear water and a nudist habit; set among dense scrub and rock Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Cala Jugadora
old.text: By car to the Cap de Creus lighthouse then 10 min down a slope path, 7 km north of Cadaques A 15 m pocket of coarse sand and gravel right under the Cap de Creus lighthouse, sheltered from the tramuntana; seabed of rock, sand tongues and Posidonia for snorkelling Open in Google Maps →
